abstract: Can a substance abuse intervention lead to sustained social ties between vulnerable women? This study analyzes the results on peer relationship outcomes of a substance abuse intervention, which included group workshops and individual and spousal counseling sessions. Using dyadic estimations, we find evidence that the intervention strengthened relationships between female peers both assigned to the treatment sixteen months post-intervention. Results were especially pronounced between pairs of treatment women in which the first had a husband with highly regressive views (generally supports wife beating) and the second woman's husband did not. Among these dyadic peer links, we find that a woman is significantly more likely to receive money from her peer, speak daily with her peer, and attend a community organization with her peer relative to those in the control. The study contributes to our understanding of methods to improve support among those who have vulnerability to IPV through building links with those less vulnerable.
abstract_zh: 物质滥用干预能否促成弱势女性之间持续的社会联系？本研究分析了一项物质滥用干预措施对同伴关系结果的影响，该干预包括小组工作坊及个人和配偶咨询会议。通过二元估计方法，我们发现有证据表明，在干预后十六个月，该干预加强了被分配至治疗组的女性同伴之间的关系。这一效果在特定配对中尤为显著：即第一方女性其丈夫持有高度倒退观点（普遍支持殴打妻子），而第二方女性的丈夫则无此观点的治疗组女性之间。在这些二元同伴联系中，我们发现，相较于对照组，一位女性显著更有可能从她的同伴那里获得金钱、每日与同伴交谈，并与同伴一同参加社区组织活动。本研究增进了我们对如何通过建立与较少受暴力风险女性的联系，来改善易受亲密伴侣暴力侵害者支持方法的理解。
title: Women Talking: Intimate Partner Violence, Group Discussions, and Their Effects on Social and Economic Ties
title_zh: 女性之声：亲密伴侣暴力、小组讨论及其对社会与经济联系的影响
